decisions.thought: Mirror team. Garchomp with Focus Sash leads well to get Stealth Rock up, and Gholdengo blocks status/spin while Kingambit cleans late. This core covers speed, priority, and setup.
Garchomp outspeeds and Earthquake is 4x effective on Kingambit, likely scoring a clean KO before it can act. Taking it out turn 1 is far better value than setting rocks.

Dragonite is immune to Earthquake and Multiscale halves Scale Shot while at full HP. Setting Stealth Rock breaks Multiscale on every future switch-in and pressures Dragonite, so it's the best value play.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Dragonite immune to EQ, Multiscale halves Scale Shot. Stealth Rock is great vs Multiscale/Dragonite.

decisions.thought: Garchomp is at 1 HP and Dragonite's Ice Spinner will KO it. Gholdengo resists Ice and walls Dragonite well, so switch out before taking the hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Dragonite faster than min? Garchomp 169 outspeeds. Dragonite at 87%, Multiscale broken. Scale Shot could KO? Weak-ish. Garchomp at 1 HP, Ice Spinner kills it. Switch to Gholdengo—immune to Ice Spinner? No, Ice Spinner is Ice, Gholdengo resists? Steel resists Ice, Ghost neutral. Good switch.

decisions.thought: I outspeed Dragonite (149 vs max 145) and its Multiscale is broken at 87%, so Make It Rain with Life Orb chunks it for roughly half or more, with a real chance to KO. Even if it survives, Ice Spinner only does reduced damage back and I easily tank it. Nasty Plot is riskier since Dragonite could Dragon Dance or pivot out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Let me analyze this turn.

My Gholdengo (134/162, 82.7%) is facing an opposing Dragonite at 87% HP with Stealth Rock on their side. Dragonite's ability is unknown — could be Multiscale (but it's at 87%, so Multiscale is broken) or Inner Focus.

Dragonite has revealed Ice Spinner. Ice Spinner is super effective vs Gholdengo? No wait — Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost. Ice is not super effective against Steel or Ghost. Actually Ice Spinner was "not very effective" against Gholdengo last turn. So Ice Spinner does reduced damage.

Gholdengo at 149 Speed vs Dragonite 90-145 — I likely outspeed but not guaranteed (Dragonite could be up to 145). Actually 149 > 145 max, so I always outspeed. Wait, the range says 90-145, and my speed is 149, so I always move first.

Make It Rain: Steel, 120 BP, Life Orb boosted. Dragonite is Dragon/Flying — Steel is super effective vs... no, Steel is not super effective vs Dragon or Flying. Steel hits Fairy, Ice, Rock. So Make It Rain is neutral vs Dragonite. 120 BP + Life Orb 1.3x = 156 effective. Gholdengo SpA 185. Neutral hit on Dragonite (SpD 108-167). That's likely a big chunk — probably around 60-75%? Let me estimate: Level 50, SpA 185, BP 120, LO 1.3x. Damage = ((2*50/5+2)*120*185/SpD)/50+2, times 1.3, times random 0.85-1. With SpD ~140: ((22)*120*185/140)/50+2 = (22*120*185)/140 = 488400/140 = 3488.6, /50 = 69.77, +2 = 71.77, *1.3 = 93.3, *0.85-1 = 79-93. Dragonite HP ~166-198, at 87% = ~144-172 HP. So Make It Rain does roughly 79-93 damage, which is about 45-55% of max HP. Dragonite at 87% (~144-172 current HP) would survive unless high roll vs low HP. Hmm, not a guaranteed KO.

Shadow Ball: Ghost 80 BP vs Dragonite — neutral (Dragon isn't immune to Ghost; Dragon/Flying takes neutral Ghost). 80 BP is weaker than Make It Rain.

Nasty Plot: Dragonite could Ice Spinner (not very effective, ~30-40 damage?) or use another move like Extreme Speed (priority, normal, neutral). Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost — Extreme Speed is Normal, immune! Dragonite commonly runs Extreme Speed. If I Nasty Plot, Dragonite could E-Speed which does nothing (Ghost immune). But it could also have Fire Punch/Earthquake? Earthquake doesn't affect... no, Gholdengo is Ghost so Ground hits it (it's not levitating — actually Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, Ground is neutral). Dragonite could have Earthquake, Fire Punch, etc.

Actually, the key question: can I KO Dragonite this turn? Make It Rain does ~45-55%, not a KO. Dragonite at 87% with Stealth Rock... it's already taken SR damage (it's at 87% which includes SR chip when it came in? It came in turn 1 after Kingambit fainted — SR was set turn 2, after Dragonite came in. Wait, turn 2: Dragonite used Ice Spinner, my Garchomp sash survived, then Stealth Rock set. So Dragonite hasn't taken SR damage yet — it's at 87% from Rough Skin chip. Next time it switches out and back in, it takes 12.5% (Dragon/Flying = neutral to Rock, 12.5%).

So Make It Rain: ~79-93 damage vs ~144-172 current HP. Not a KO. Then Dragonite hits back with Ice Spinner (not very effective, ~35-45 damage?) — Gholdengo survives fine.

Alternatively, Nasty Plot to boost, then Make It Rain next turn would KO. But Dragonite might switch out (taking SR) or hit me. Ice Spinner does reduced damage to Gholdengo. What else could Dragonite have? Common sets: Dragonite with Ice Spinner, Extreme Speed, Earthquake/Fire Punch, Dragon Dance. If it has Dragon Dance, it might boost too.

Actually, wait — could Make It Rain KO with Stealth Rock? No, SR only triggers on switch-in.

Let me reconsider: Dragonite HP range 166-198. At 87%: 144-172. Make It Rain damage: let me recompute more carefully.

Gholdengo SpA 185 (given stat). Level 50. Make It Rain 120 BP, Life Orb 1.3x, neutral effectiveness.

Damage formula: (((2*Level/5 + 2) * BP * A/D)/50 + 2) * modifiers
2*50/5+2 = 22.
A = SpA stat = 185 (this includes nature? The stat given is presumably final). D = opponent SpD, range 108-167.

Min damage case: D=167: 22*120*185/167 = 488400/167 = 2924.6, /50 = 58.5, +2 = 60.5, *1.3 = 78.6, *0.85 = 66.8.
Max damage case: D=108: 22*120*185/108 = 488400/108 = 4522, /50 = 90.4, +2 = 92.4, *1.3 = 120.2, *1.0 = 120.

So damage range roughly 67-120. Dragonite current HP 144-172. So KO chance exists if Dragonite is low SpD and I roll high, but not guaranteed. Probably ~30-40% KO chance? Hmm.

If not KO'd, Dragonite hits back. Ice Spinner vs Gholdengo: Ice vs Steel = not very effective (0.5x), vs Ghost = neutral. So 0.5x. Dragonite Atk 138-204, BP 80. Damage: 22*80*Atk/Def(Gholdengo 115)/50+2. With Atk 170: 22*80*170/115 = 299200/115 = 2601.7, /50 = 52, +2 = 54, *0.5 = 27, *0.85-1 = 23-27. Gholdengo at 134 HP survives easily.

But Dragonite might have Extreme Speed (priority +2, Normal — immune vs Ghost). Or Earthquake (neutral, ~54-70 damage?). Or Dragon Dance.

The safest strong play: Make It Rain now, chunk Dragonite hard, possibly KO. If it survives, it's in Make It Rain range next turn (plus SR if it switches).

Alternatively Nasty Plot: boost +2, but Dragonite could DD alongside, or switch to a special wall. Gholdengo with NP +2 Make It Rain would likely sweep. But risk: Dragonite could KO? Ice Spinner only does ~25. E-Speed immune. So Nasty Plot is quite safe this turn actually. But then next turn Make It Rain at +2: damage doubles-ish (×2 from +2 SpA): 134-240, guaranteed KO on Dragonite (max 198 HP... wait current 144-172, +2 damage 134-240 — mostly KO but low roll vs high HP might not: 134 vs 172? No wait, if Dragonite has high HP (198 max, 87% = 172 current) and my damage is at low end 134... hmm, +2 SpA means A = 185*2 = 370 effectively (stat stage doubling). Damage = 22*120*370/D/50+2. With D=167: 22*120*370/167 = 976800/167 = 5849, /50 = 117, +2 = 119, *1.3 = 154.7, *0.85 = 131.5. vs 172 current HP — not a KO! Hmm. With D=140: 22*120*370/140 = 976800/140 = 6977, /50 = 139.5, +2 = 141.5, *1.3 = 184, *0.85 = 156. vs 172 — not guaranteed.

Hmm, so even +2 Make It Rain isn't a guaranteed KO on a bulky Dragonite. Interesting.

But wait — Dragonite's SpD range 108-167. A typical Dragonite isn't specially bulky; likely SpD around 110-130. With D=120: 22*120*185/120 = 488400/120 = 4070, /50 = 81.4, +2 = 83.4, *1.3 = 108.4, *0.85-1 = 92-108. Current HP 144-172 (if HP is 166-198). So not a KO guaranteed, but chunks ~55-65%.

Hmm, what about the fact that Dragonite is at 87% — that's after Rough Skin chip (1/8 = 12.5%). So it took one contact hit. Its max HP: if it's at 87% after losing 12.5%, max HP could be anything.

Decision: Make It Rain is the aggressive play — big chunk, possible KO, and Steel STAB. The SpA drop (-2) is a downside but Gholdengo's special attack is still usable, and I have Nasty Plot to recover boosts. Actually Make It Rain lowering SpA by 2 is significant — after one Make It Rain, my SpA drops to effectively half. Then subsequent Make It Rains are weak.

Alternative: Shadow Ball — 80 BP, no self-drop, but weaker (80 vs 120*1.3=156 effective... Make It Rain effective BP with LO is 156; Shadow Ball with LO is 104). Make It Rain is clearly stronger even accounting for the drop.

What about the opponent's remaining team? Opponent brought 3: Kingambit (fainted), Dragonite, and 1 more from garchomp, gholdengo, rotomwash, sylveon. So their third is one of those. Sylveon would be hit hard by Make It Rain (Steel vs Fairy super effective). Rotom-Wash resists Steel (Water/Electric — Steel is resisted? Steel vs Water = 0.5x? No — Steel vs Water is neutral... actually Steel is not very effective against Water? Let me recall: Steel is super effective vs Ice, Rock, Fairy; not very effective vs Fire, Water, Electric, Steel. Yes, Steel is resisted by Water and Electric. So Rotom-W resists Make It Rain.)

Given Dragonite is the current threat and I outspeed, Make It Rain is the best immediate action. It chunks Dragonite ~50-65%, possibly KO. Even if it survives, Dragonite is badly hurt and I can finish later. The SpA drop is manageable.

Actually, let me reconsider Nasty Plot more. The threat assessment: Dragonite's Ice Spinner does ~25 to me. I'm at 134/162. Even Earthquake (~55-70) doesn't threaten me much. E-Speed is immune. So I'm quite safe against Dragonite regardless. Nasty Plot sets up a sweep potential. But the opponent's unknown third Pokémon could be Rotom-Wash (burns? Will-O-Wisp doesn't affect... Gholdengo is immune to status via Good as Gold! Status moves can't affect Gholdengo). So Gholdengo is immune to status moves entirely. Rotom-W's Hydro Pump would hurt though.

But the instruction says choose the single best action. Make It Rain now: deals big damage, and if Dragonite stays, I can Make It Rain again (at -2 SpA, damage ~half: 46-60, then Dragonite at ~87% - 55% - 30% = dead-ish). Hmm, actually with the -2 drop, follow-up Make It Rains are weak.

Let me think about what maximizes value. Dragonite at 87%, likely to switch out soon anyway (it took Rough Skin chip, faces SR on re-entry). If I Nasty Plot and it switches, I get a free +2 and can then Make It Rain the incoming Pokémon. If I Make It Rain and it switches, I wasted the SpA drop on a chunk.

But Make It Rain might just KO (30-50% chance). And Dragonite could DD up while I NP, making it dangerous for my Kingambit/Garchomp later. Dragonite at +1 with Ice Spinner threatens Garchomp (4x weak to Ice) — though Garchomp is at 0.5% anyway, basically dead.

Hmm. Kingambit is my win condition (Sucker Punch, Kowtow Cleave, Supreme Overlord with 2-3 fallen allies). Dragonite resists Dark? No — Dark vs Dragon/Flying is neutral. Kingambit's Sucker Punch vs Dragonite: Atk 205, BP 70 priority. 22*70*205/Def(~130)/50+2 = 22*70*205 = 315700/130 = 2428.5, /50 = 48.6, +2 = 50.6, *0.85-1 = 43-50. Not huge.

I think the straightforward best play is Make It Rain — it's the strongest immediate action, likely 2HKO or better, and Gholdengo outspeeds and tanks Ice Spinner fine. The SpA drop matters less because Kingambit is the cleaner.

Actually, one more consideration: could Dragonite have Multiscale? It's at 87%, so Multiscale is broken — no halving. Good.

Also, is there a chance Dragonite outspeeds and... it can't KO me with anything revealed. Even if it has Fire Punch (super effective vs Steel): 22*80*170/115/50+2 = 54, *2 = 108, *0.85-1 = 92-108. That would hurt (134 HP — survive barely at low roll? 92-108 vs 134 — survive). Hmm, Fire Punch max 108 < 134, survive. OK.

Make It Rain it is.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is at 3% and we outspeed, so any decent hit KOs. With SpA at -2, Shadowball actually outdamages Make It Rain right now and avoids stacking more drops. Shadowball secures the knockout cleanly.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite is at 3% HP. Gholdengo has Make It Rain at 120 BP with Life Orb, but SpA is -2. Even with -2, Make It Rain should easily KO Dragonite at 3%. Shadowball at 80 BP with 0 SpA boost might also KO, but Make It Rain is more reliable. Actually, let me think - Make It Rain with -2 SpA: 120 BP * 0.5 (from -2) = effectively 60 BP, plus Life Orb 1.3x = ~78 BP effective, STAB 1.5x = ~117. Against 3% HP Dragonite, that's definitely a KO. Shadowball: 80 BP, STAB 1.5x = 120, Life Orb 1.3x = 156 effective, no SpA drop. That's even stronger than Make It Rain right now due to the -2 drop. Wait - could Dragonite have priority? Ice Spinner is +0. Dragonite could have Extreme Speed if it had it, but only Ice Spinner revealed. Multiscale doesn't matter at 3%.

Make It Rain would drop SpA to -4, which is bad for future. Shadowball is the better choice - stronger due to no drop, and might drop SpD.

Actually wait, Make It Rain at -2: 120 * 0.5 = 60 base power equivalent... Actually stat stage -2 = 2/3 damage? No: -1 = 2/3? Let me recall: +1 = 1.5x, +2 = 2x, -1 = 0.66x, -2 = 0.5x. Yes, -2 = 0.5x.

Make It Rain: 120 * 0.5 * 1.5 (STAB) * 1.3 (LO) = 117 effective.
Shadowball: 80 * 1 * 1.5 * 1.3 = 156 effective.

Shadowball is stronger. Both KO 3% Dragonite guaranteed. Shadowball preserves SpA and has chance to drop SpD. Choose Shadowball.

Also consider: Dragonite could switch? No, it's the opponent's turn to move; they might switch but we can't predict. Shadowball is safe.

Decision: MOVE: shadowball

decisions.thought: Shadow Ball was super effective and left their Gholdengo at 29% with a SpD drop; another Shadow Ball with Life Orb should finish it, while Make It Rain is resisted. Speed is close but even if they move first, they can't KO me from 48%.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Shadow Ball again likely KOs (last one did big damage). Make It Rain is resisted. Shadow Ball.
